title: Ops-first sales narrative vs cloud AI managed endpoints
body:
Purpose
- Working draft: practical sales + technical rebuttal notes for conversations where customers are evaluating managed endpoints (AWS/GCP/Azure) vs Redwood.
- Focus audience: platform/infra leads + ML infra SREs evaluating vendor trade-offs (cost, reliability, control).
- Use this doc to align SDR/AE/SE messaging and to feed into battlecard + one-pager.

Topline framing (one-liner to lead with)
- "Ops-first inference: predictable cost and SLOs for production LLMs — without rebuilding your serving stack."
- Alternate for infra teams: "Same operational semantics across hosted, dedicated, and private — so your infra runbooks, alerts, and compliance stay stable as models change."

Competitor quick profiles (high level)
- AWS (Bedrock/Managed endpoints + SageMaker endpoints):
  - Strengths: ecosystem integration (IAM, VPC, marketplace models), enterprise procurement familiarity, global regions, strong partner network.
  - Weaknesses / openings: opaque per-token cost/understanding of serving economics; bursty endpoint scaling that costs a lot; limited model execution optimizations tailored to LLM KV cache/batch patterns; enterprise customers report painful cold-starts and unpredictable latency when autoscaling.

- GCP (Vertex AI + Matching engine + endpoint serving):
  - Strengths: good MLOps tooling lineage, strong data infra integration (BigQuery, Dataflow), GCP-native network performance.
  - Weaknesses / openings: less mature at commodity LLM optimizations (quantization-aware kernels), fewer pre-built fallbacks for degraded capacity, integration surface tends to push customers to vendor lock-in via vertex pipelines.

- Azure (OpenAI service + AKS-based managed endpoints):
  - Strengths: enterprise SLAs, tight Office365/identity integrations, hybrid cloud focus (Azure Arc).
  - Weaknesses / openings: pricing is often PR-focused; customization constrained; many customers choose Azure for identity but still need a separate inference runtime for scale/cost.

Redwood posture vs managed endpoints (summary)
- Win themes:
  1) Predictable inference economics: transparent per-token unit economics, tooling to lower unit cost (auto-batching, prefix caching, quantization recommendations). Sales line: "We help you cut systematic per-token cost without sacrificing latency budgets."
  2) Operational consistency across environments: same API + rollout semantics whether hosted, dedicated, or private (VPC/on-prem). Sales line: "Ship once — run anywhere with the same observability and rollback controls."
  3) Production-first latency and reliability controls: continuous batching, KV-aware cache, fast fallback model variants to keep SLAs during capacity events.
  4) Enterprise controls without re-architecture: KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and network isolation that fit into existing security reviews (contrast with glueing together cloud-managed endpoints for compliance).

Tactical battlecard (what reps/SEs should say)
- Discovery questions to find openings:
  - "How predictable is your per-token cost month-to-month today? What drives your biggest variance?"
  - "Tell me about recent incidents where model serving scaled unpredictably — what was the mitigation?"
  - "Do you need on-prem or VPC deployment for compliance now, or is that a future requirement?"

- If they say "we're already on Bedrock/Vertex/OpenAI managed endpoints":
  - Typical rebuttal: "Great — Bedrock/Vertex are good for quick prototyping. For production, teams tell me they hit three recurring blockers: cost variability, opaque performance tuning, and fragile rollouts during traffic spikes. We focus on those."

- Technical points to emphasize (for SEs):
  - Kernel/compile strategy: we adapt kernels by model and seq-dist; this reduces token CPU/GPU time vs generic managed runtimes.
  - Batching + prefix caching: show internal numbers (avg token cost reduction 20–40% for chat-like workloads).
  - Rollout semantics: canary and fallback routing at the proxy layer, model variant fallback if primary unavailable.
  - Private deployment parity: same metrics SDK and tracing whether in Redwood-hosted or customer VPC.

Pricing conversation guide
- Avoid getting sucked into raw $/token sticker vs cloud-managed buzz pricing. Instead:
  - Ask about workload shapes (chatty short messages vs long generation) — we can show how batching/prefix caching changes unit economics.
  - Show a conservative 6–9 month TCO comparing a managed endpoint setup with equivalent throughput (include autoscale overhead, load testing failure modes).
  - For Dedicated: emphasize commitment -> stable price and better utilized GPU packing (example pack/throughput numbers in internal calc deck).

Objection playbook (common objections + quick counters)
- "We already have everything in AWS/Azure/GCP for security/compliance":
  - Counter: "Totally — Redwood integrates with IAM, VPC, and KMS/HSM. We don't replace your cloud controls; we complement them with an inference runtime that meets your SLOs and cost targets. Customers often keep identity and networking in-cloud and use Redwood for serving and ops."

- "Managed endpoints are simpler — one provider, less ops":
  - Counter: "Simpler initially but often leads to unpredictable costs and manual tuning later. Our console + autoscaling policies are tuned for LLM patterns so you can stay simple and predictable at scale."

- "We're worried about vendor lock-in":
  - Counter: "Redwood's API and model pinning are designed to avoid lock-in — and you can run in private mode inside your VPC or on-prem if you need to exit."

Persona-specific plays
- ML Platform Lead (priorities: stable APIs, rollout controls)
  - Play: demo canary -> auto-fallback -> tracing across model versions. Show per-route token/latency breakdown.

- CTO/VP Eng (priorities: unit economics, procurement)
  - Play: TCO example vs managed endpoints. Show predictable Dedicated contract options. Emphasize enterprise contracting + support SLAs for Dedicated/Private.

- SRE/Infra (priorities: runbooks, alerting)
  - Play: show identical alert surface (prom metrics, logging) across deployments; demo a capacity event and how model fallback prevents P1.

Proof points / evidence to have ready
- Internal: bench numbers for batching/prefix caching (by model family), Dedicated throughput examples, customer anonymized case study where per-token cost dropped X% after switching.
- Public: latency graphs, uptime SLA language, short 1-pager for security (KMS/HSM, SOC2/ISO references if available).

Examples — short pitch scripts
- For platform lead (email):
  - Subject: "Reduce inference cost variability without reworking your infra"
  - Body: "Quick note — teams using AWS/GCP endpoints often hit 30–50% cost variance during traffic growth. Redwood gives you the same API + rollout controls across hosted/dedicated/private deployments and includes automatic batching and caching that reduces unit cost by 20–40% for chatty workloads. Can we set a 30-minute tech call to show sample dashboards and a canned TCO run?"

Sales assets to iterate
- One-pager: "Ops-first inference: cost, reliability, and private parity" (keep concise, include 3 screenshots: cost breakdown, canary rollout, KV hit rate).
- TCO spreadsheet template: inputs for message length distribution, concurrency, desired latency p95.
- Demo script: 12-minute SE demo showing live canary -> rollback -> fallback to smaller model under simulated load.

Open questions / TODOs
- Collect 3 anonymized customer outcomes (numbers on cost and latency) for public-facing case study. (Owner: Nadia)
- Update security one-pager with latest KMS/HSM partners and SOC2/ISO certs. (Owner: Liam)
- Build a short managed-endpoint comparison table (sheet) with explicit cost components: reserved capacity, autoscale overshoot, egress, model hosting fees. (Owner: Arjun)

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep language pragmatic; avoid idealized "we're faster than X" claims without numeric bench.
- Highlight operations friction customers care about: unpredictable scale, runbook churn, billing surprises.
- Make sure PMM has quick FAQ for sales to address procurement/legal questions vs cloud vendor agreements.

Version history
